The Stripper removes CO from the loaded solvent by contacting the rich solvent flowing down the vessel 2 with water vapor and CO rising from the reboiler at the vessel bottom. Water vapor condenses into the 2 loaded solvent stream, where the heat of condensation provides the energy to reverse the chemical reaction between the CO and the solvent, releasing CO into the vapor phase. 2 2 The product gas leaving the Stripper is relatively hot at about 130°F and is saturated with water vapor. The Overhead Condenser utilizes a heat exchanger set fed by water from the CW system to reduce the temperature to about 90°F. Condensation from this reduction in temperature removes most of the water vapor, leaving a 99% pure stream of CO product gas to continue to compression. The water removed from 2 the product gas is returned to the lean solvent flow downstream of the LRX. After the solvent has been regenerated in the Stripper, the Stripper Lean Pumps send the hot-lean solvent through the LRX and into the top of the Absorber. A slipstream of the lean solvent flows through an Activated Carbon Filtration System. A slipstream from the Carbon Filtration System goes through an additional Electrodialysis Reclaiming System (EDR) to remove heat-stable salts. At the bottom of the Stripper, low-grade steam (tube-side) indirectly heats the solvent (shell-side) via the once-through Thermosyphon Steam Heaters to release CO and water vapor from the solvent. The water 2 vapor released from the solvent re-condenses throughout the Stripper by counter-currently contacting the hot-lean and cold-rich solvent, respectively, thus evolving the remainder of absorbed CO while minimizing 2 Steam Heater duty. The steam condensate is returned to the BOP Steam System. The CO -lean solvent 2 recycles to the Absorber through the Lean-Rich Heat Exchanger and Trim Cooler for further capture. The solvent breaks down slowly through regular operation, and this system requires a make-up solvent to be added to maintain solvent effectiveness. Virgin solvent is stored in the Solvent Make-Up Tank and added to the system as necessary. The CO exits the top of the Stripper to the Integrally Geared CO Compressor Train. The compressed, dried, 2 2 supercritical CO condenses to a dense-phase product (over 0.3 s.g.) and pumps into a double wall pipeline 2 for final sequestration or CO EOR. Some solvent is removed from the CO gas by the cooler. The 2 2 Dehydration System removes water from the CO gas upstream of the HP compressor to meet pipeline 2 specifications.
